note: Authored teaching scenario. The item counts are the real counts of published archive records (see /archive/); the sizes for print and image are the real figures from earlier packs (week 4's retained listing; transcription files are a few KB). Audio's size is an estimate, labelled as such, because no audio bytes are currently published for that collection. The dollar rates are fictional, stated so a student can recompute every total.

revisedRates.note: Source-tier labor revised upward from $12 to $20 per item, reflecting that full byte-level preservation now includes a per-item provenance audit of the kind week 11 actually required — a cost the original $12 figure did not account for.

families.label: Print
families.note: The 11 published print records: the card and its three photocopy generations, the digital control, the ordinance, and its five witnesses. Each is a short transcription, a few KB.

families.label: Audio
families.note: The 5 published audio records (source, W, X, Y, Z). No audio bytes are currently published for this collection — the archive holds only feature tables, by policy. A source tier here means preserving real audio bytes for the first time, estimated at 30 seconds of CD-quality WAV per item (roughly 5.2 MB), not a measurement of an actual retained file.

families.label: Image
families.note: The 2 published image records: the 2400x1600 source (11,240 KB, per week 4's retained working-directory listing) and Output 7 (148 KB).

proposals.label: Deep image, thin everything else
proposals.summary: Bring the image family to full source-tier preservation. Hold print and audio at examples tier.

proposals.label: Start preserving real audio
proposals.summary: Hold print and image at examples tier. Spend the remaining budget bringing as much of the audio family as affordable to source tier — the first real audio bytes this archive would retain — leaving the rest at examples.

objection.text: The image family already carries a documented, partly-inferred provenance gap (week 11's audit). Spending the budget there polishes an already-uncertain record instead of creating coverage where there is currently none, such as real audio bytes.
objection.response: This does not settle which proposal is better; it names what the naive value score in this pack cannot see. Full source-tier preservation of the image family also buys something the score does not count: byte-level material for week 11's kind of audit to be run on again later, on a family that already has a documented gap worth closing. Starting real audio preservation buys first coverage for a family with none. A memo has to say which of those it is choosing to weight higher, not appeal to a total that averages the two questions away.
